title: I too made a game in four days for the Epic AI Mega Game Jam using Astra & Fable
author: frostybaby13
selftext:
I too made a game in four days for the Unreal AI Mega Game Jam. And I used GPT 6 Astra and Codex and also Fable 5.2 and Opus 5.5. And a lot of credits for 3D models came from the Megajam partners, and voices & sound effects from Eleven Labs.  
  
The game has four sort of unique biomes to explore: a night forest, a haunted laundromat, a snowy forest, and a giant office building. And then there are some secret scattered wells hidden in the forest that have an MIB monitor hiding inside spying, and cabins filled with cats, and a cat lady that if you find her, she'll give you one of her cats, which happens to be a big, beautiful dog that can be your archer's pet for the rest of the game.  
  
What I learned after this experience was that although you can make the most beautiful things with AI now, especially coming from an art background... when I first made the very first forest, I looked at the screenshots that the AI showed me and I was like, "Woah! This is so beautiful!! This is, this is better than Skyrim!!" And then I went into the forest and I was like, oh no, this is really boring. There's nothing to do. And so that really pushed me to try to figure out the implementation of some survival elements because I had a story in mind that I wanted to tell going to these different locations and having this reveal. But the gameplay to get through that story needed to be fun.   
  
That's, I think, what I learned because I've always, always daydreamed stories and I have always been able to draw and do art (just not digital art). I know how to make things pretty. And being an early adopter of AI, I know how to push AI to make pretty things for me too. But what I don't know how to do, even though I'm a huge gamer, is make gameplay fun.   
  
That was the real, the huge thing to try to work on during this game jam. And I found it difficult because how could I explain to Fable 5.2, who's 50 times smarter than me, how to make an archery system more fun? How to make the shots more impactful? I could say things like, well, the trees are getting in the way of the shots and that's really going to make a player mad. But I couldn't say the shot doesn't feel like it has any weight to it or this is just not fun. There's not enough... the animals aren't attacking you! There's no challenge! You don't get hurt enough! It was very hard to articulate those things in a way that the AI could then take that and turn it into numbers and then make the gameplay better. So unfortunately in a four-day game jam, you don't have enough time to get in there and play and keep saying like, okay, this part's too hard, this part's too easy. So, surprise, nothing in this game is too hard - it's too easy, I find. The only hard part comes when you're supposed to hunt foxes, the second quest activity that you get to do. And there are only seven foxes on this huge map. Of course they respawn, which is nice. But if you're wandering the map, that might be frustrating for a player.   
  
AI, at least in my experience, at least right now, definitely tend toward making things too easy. So that would be a challenge in the future. I think if you were making a game seriously - going in and playing it and figuring out how to articulate what you needed back to the AI in more of a technical manner would be the biggest challenge for ME. But it was an awesome experience as someone who's always loved video games and never had the technical ability to make them. This was really fun!!   
  
And my page on Itch is really plain and junky looking because I spent all my time doing the game. And now I'm scared to touch it because I don't know if it'll disqualify you if you do anything to make your itch page prettier after submission. But I see so many other people's pretty itch pages and I'm very jealous. Anyway, here she is:
